teaser: Update 2: the story held, the site watches its own readers privately, agents run on a schedule, and decisions wait on me.
core_idea: On 23 October the php2shell story held its key line, no named compromise, while the newsroom covering it moved to scheduled agents, pack-mode vaults and self-observation, and the main constraint became the editor's decisions.

figures.caption: The PHP site's telemetry dashboard (v0.4.0) on 23 October: 1,093 page views from 13:43 UTC on 22 October to 20:26 UTC on 23 October, split into readers, the editor, power users and the team, synthetic readers and crawlers, with every chart and number a filter. Here: readers in the United Kingdom, phones left out, in three clicks.
All 1,093 page views by group: 233 by readers in 168 sessions, 110 by the editor, 9 by power users and the team, 176 synthetic, 565 by crawlers.
Page views per hour from 13:00 on 22 October to 20:00 on 23 October, by group: the crawler working through the night, readers steadiest in the UK morning and afternoon.
Readers by country, on a log scale: eighteen countries, the United Kingdom first by far, then the United States and Norway.
How reader sessions move through the PHP site, step by step: most start on the front page, and most of those end there, at the grey block marked (left).
The same moves as a network: each page a node sized by the sessions that saw it. The front page is the hub; the one route that bypasses it runs from a source page to the claims.
What works, page by page: right is read more, up is where readers go on. The front page is far right and low: read most, sending about one in five on.
Exploring the PHP story's risk graph from one node: from CVE-2026-109618 to the fix, the tests that check it and the risks it touches, with inferred links dashed and hideable.

What the risk graph is missing, computed at every release over its 713 nodes and 1,418 edges: 95 of 95 controls joined to no code or test, 16 of 16 code nodes with no owner one step away, 9 of 16 that no test reaches, 14 of 34 risks no story tells, and 815 links inferred by an agent and not yet checked.
Mockup A of the PHP site's redesign, for review: a board member's front page with the Focus, Standard and Everything dial and an answer in thirty seconds. Not the live site.
